territorial_scope.description: Applies to federal agencies defined in 44 U.S.C. 3502(1) and excludes the Intelligence Community and National Security Systems.

evidence.quote: Except as specifically noted, this memorandum applies to all agencies defined in 44 U.S.C. § 3502(1).

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Sets requirements and recommendations for US federal agencies acquiring AI systems and services, covering market research, solicitation disclosures, contract terms on IP, data, privacy, vendor lock-in and testing. Applies to contracts from solicitations issued 180 days after issuance onward.
summary.long: Issued under Executive Order 13960 and the Advancing American AI Act, and consistent with OMB Memorandum M-25-21, this memorandum guides agencies in acquiring AI systems or services and rescinds and replaces M-24-18. It applies to agencies defined in 44 U.S.C. 3502(1), with CFO Act agencies covered by some requirements, and excludes the Intelligence Community, national security systems, and AI used incidentally by contractors, among other exclusions. Agencies must update acquisition procedures within 270 days. Where practicable, they must disclose in solicitations whether a planned use meets the high-impact use case threshold. Contracts must include terms on IP rights and government data, including a permanent bar on using nonpublic agency data to train publicly or commercially available AI absent explicit agency consent, and on privacy, vendor lock-in protections and ongoing testing. Agencies must test proposed solutions to the greatest extent practicable and obtain an authorization to operate before deployment. GSA must develop acquisition guides within 100 days and a shared repository within 200 days. The memorandum does not specify penalties.

notes: The OCR text renders OMB as '0MB' throughout; quotes are kept as printed. Appendix 1 is omitted from the source text. Internal cross-reference errors: Sec. 4(d)(iii)(B) points to Sec. 3(c) for privacy, but privacy is Sec. 3(d); Sec. 4(d)(iii)(G) cites Sec. 3(g) for new feature notification, but Sec. 3(g) concerns a shared repository. The guidance is non-binding in form (requirements are often 'should' or 'encouraged'). Section 2(c) applies the memorandum to contracts from 180 days after issuance. thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changes legal treatment in this text. The 180-day applicability date (Sec. 2(c)) and the 100-, 200- and 270-day deadlines (Sec. 3(b), 3(f), 3(g)) are time limits coded as events. The high-impact AI use case is defined by reference to M-25-21 without a number, and CFO Act agency status is defined by reference to 31 U.S.C. § 901(b).
